memory_candidates.content: When bulk-clearing task-number citations in a docs/ tree gated by a mechanical grep-based check (e.g. check-module-invariants.sh's C9D), do not trust a research report's per-file breakdown as exhaustive -- the report's own count list is often truncated (e.g. 'top 5' files) and the full regex re-run after each file's fix routinely surfaces additional unassigned files carrying the remaining citations. Budget an extra pass per phase to re-run the exact enforcement regex (not just the itemized files) and clear what it finds, tracking the extra work as a plan deviation rather than leaving the phase closed with the mechanical gate still red.

A bare `cloc --include-lang=Lean --exclude-dir=.lake,lake-packages,Boneyard .` run from the repo root over-counts the live library when the repo also has specs/ task-artifact scratch files and .claude/ test fixtures containing .lean files -- these are swept in despite the exclude-dir list because they live under directories named neither .lake, lake-packages, nor Boneyard. Scope the cloc invocation to the actual library roots (e.g. `cloc --include-lang=Lean --exclude-dir=Boneyard FormalSystem Tests`) to match what the project's own structural-invariant script counts as 'live'.

When implementing a task concurrently with sibling tasks that touch the same shared files (e.g. a package/naming migration), re-read ground truth (grep the actual config file, e.g. lakefile.toml's `name =` line) rather than trusting the plan's naming assumption before writing a naming key or cross-reference -- the plan may have been authored before the sibling task's migration landed, and the sibling's commit history (git log --oneline -- <file>) shows whether it already completed.
